summary: Single deployable monolith: Blazor (ASP.NET Core), C# + ASP.NET Core, Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL database on Azure Container Apps. It keeps data in Indian regions, matches the team's languages and is estimated at $78-$190 per month.

architecture.name: monolith
architecture.justification: One deployable is the fastest to build and simplest to run for a team of 2 and 1 feature area (file storage).

alternatives.why_not: Adds service boundaries, network calls and per-service deployment that this team does not need at this scale (team 2).
Per-request functions suit light, spiky work; this backend runs as a long-lived service on Azure Container Apps, which suits websockets, background jobs and steady traffic better.

frontend.justification: Blazor (ASP.NET Core) matches the team's csharp skills; C# end to end, component model, reuses Entra auth; is a proven choice for internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Vue 3 + Vite (SPA) scores 0.9 points lower overall, mainly on compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.6 points) and team skill fit (0.4 points).
Angular scores 1.2 points lower overall, mainly on budget fit (1.3 points) and team skill fit (1.1 points). Estimated infrastructure about $180-$360/month versus about $77-$170/month.

tradeoffs: Server mode ties UI to a live connection

backend.justification: C# + ASP.NET Core matches the team's csharp skills; reuses your existing Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft 365; strong typing and LTS releases; is a proven choice for internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Next.js route handlers (serverless) scores 6.8 points lower overall, mainly on reuse of existing systems (5.0 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.9 points).
Node.js + NestJS scores 7.2 points lower overall, mainly on reuse of existing systems (5.0 points) and security (1.0 points).

database.choice: Azure SQL Database in Central India (Pune)
database.justification: Microsoft SQL Server reuses your existing SQL Server; can be placed in Central India (Pune) to keep data in India; great tooling, Entra ID auth; is a proven choice for internal tool projects. It runs as Azure SQL Database, the managed service on the same cloud as the application, so backups, patching and failover are the provider's job.

alternatives.why_not: PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted) scores 2.1 points lower overall, mainly on reuse of existing systems (3.5 points) and budget fit (0.5 points).
MySQL (managed or self-hosted) scores 3.6 points lower overall, mainly on reuse of existing systems (3.5 points) and security (0.5 points).

hosting.justification: Azure Container Apps reuses your existing Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft 365; runs on AZURE as preferred; can be placed in Central India (Pune) to keep data in India; offers a 99.95% SLA, in line with the 99.9% target.

alternatives.why_not: Azure App Service scores 0.27 points higher, which is inside the near-tie range, and loses the tie-break: lower cost first, then complexity and operations load.
Azure Virtual Machines scores 4.9 points lower overall, mainly on reuse of existing systems (1.5 points) and operations load (1.2 points).

supporting.justification: Microsoft Entra ID (workforce SSO): users sign in (enterprise sso); workforce single sign-on with conditional access; the free tier covers SSO for apps; reuses your existing Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft 365; free at this scale.

alternatives.why_not: Ranks lower (lower quality rating (6 vs 9)); score 0.44 vs 0.90.

tradeoffs: Ties sign-in to the Microsoft tenant; external users need guest setup

supporting.justification: Azure Blob Storage: users upload files; object storage native to Azure; free at this scale.

alternatives.why_not: Ranks lower (lower quality rating (8 vs 9), more to operate); score 0.74 vs 0.90.

tradeoffs: Egress and transaction charges add up for media-heavy apps

supporting.choice: Microsoft Graph (Outlook mail and Teams messages)
supporting.justification: Microsoft Graph (Outlook mail and Teams messages): the approval steps in the description notify requesters and approvers; sends approval mail and Teams messages from the organisation's own Microsoft 365 tenant, so no separate email provider or domain setup is needed; free at this scale.

alternatives.why_not: Ranks lower (lower quality rating (7 vs 8)); score 0.83 vs 0.88.

tradeoffs: Needs an app registration with admin-consented mail permissions; scope it to one sending mailbox with an application access policy

supporting.justification: GitHub Actions: automated build and deploy for the team; workflows next to the code; the 2,000 free minutes a month cover a small team, larger teams buy extra minutes; free at this scale.

alternatives.why_not: Ranks lower (lower quality rating (8 vs 9), costs more (about $26 vs $0 per month at the high end), more to operate); score 0.80 vs 0.84.
Ranks lower (lower quality rating (8 vs 9), costs more (about $25 vs $0 per month at the high end), more to operate); score 0.73 vs 0.84.

tradeoffs: Minute limits on private repositories; long builds need paid or self-hosted runners

supporting.justification: Azure Monitor / Application Insights: production monitoring for the availability target; native monitoring with strong .NET diagnostics.

alternatives.why_not: Ranks lower (lower quality rating (6 vs 8)); score 0.59 vs 0.80.

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 30 requests/second and about 3.4M requests/month from 1.5K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.9% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.

breakdown.item: Microsoft Graph (Outlook mail and Teams messages)

warnings.message: SQL Server 2017 / 2019: Still supported but past mainstream support (2019: mainstream ended 2025-02-28, security fixes until 2030-01-08; 2017: security fixes until 2027-10-12). Plan the upgrade or a move to a managed SQL service as part of this project.

ISO 27001 audits your own controls (access reviews, change management, logging, incident response); vendors with their own ISO 27001 report shorten the audit, and gaps in the chosen stack are listed separately.

CERT-In directions (April 2022) apply to services used in India: enable logs on all systems, keep them for 180 days within India, sync clocks to an NTP source and report cyber incidents within 6 hours. Size log retention and storage for this.

Microsoft Entra ID / Microsoft 365 is reused through Azure Container Apps, C# + ASP.NET Core and Microsoft Entra ID (workforce SSO). Existing Entra ID tenant: reuse it for sign-in instead of a second identity system.
SQL Server is reused through C# + ASP.NET Core and Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL. Existing SQL Server data: keep it as the system of record or connect to it (hybrid connectivity or data sync).
Microsoft Azure is reused through Azure Container Apps. Existing Azure footprint.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
No cache layer: about 30 requests/second and 1,500 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.
No queue: background work is light enough for the backend or the provider's own webhooks and functions.

pipeline: filter each layer by hard constraints

relaxed_constraints: No cache layer: about 30 requests/second and 1,500 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.
No queue: background work is light enough for the backend or the provider's own webhooks and functions.

robustness.summary: The same stack wins in 12 of 14 checks. It switches to Azure App Service (hosting) when time to market counted twice as much, budget doubled ($600). The runner-up scores 0.27 points higher but costs more, and stacks within 0.75 points count as a tie that the cheaper one wins.

trade_off_options.title: Spend less
trade_off_options.gains: about 20% cheaper on the core layers plus required supporting services ($55-$140 against $77-$170 per month)
trade_off_options.summary: Database Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL -> Azure Cosmos DB: about 20% cheaper on the core layers plus required supporting services ($55-$140 against $77-$170 per month). Gives up 6.0 points, mainly on reuse of existing systems (-3.5 pts), vendor lock-in (-2.2 pts), time to market (-0.4 pts).

trade_off_options.title: More headroom to scale
trade_off_options.note: Nothing within 12 points of the winner does clearly better here, so the chosen stack is already a strong pick on this.

trade_off_options.title: Ship sooner
gives_up: compatibility with the rest of the stack (-0.6 pts)
trade_off_options.summary: Frontend Blazor (ASP.NET Core) -> Electron; hosting Azure Container Apps -> Azure App Service: time to market 8.2 instead of 7.4. Gives up 1.7 points, mainly on budget fit (-1.3 pts), compatibility with the rest of the stack (-0.6 pts), cost (-0.6 pts).

trade_off_options.title: Less vendor lock-in
trade_off_options.summary: Frontend Blazor (ASP.NET Core) -> Vue 3 + Vite (SPA); database Microsoft SQL Server / Azure SQL -> PostgreSQL (managed or self-hosted); hosting Azure Container Apps -> Azure Virtual Machines: lock-in 1.8 instead of 3.5 (0-10 scale). Gives up 7.7 points, mainly on reuse of existing systems (-5.0 pts), budget fit (-1.4 pts), operations load (-1.2 pts).
